summary: Defines an extension to the Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol (DLEP) that lets a modem report the range of latency that can be experienced on a link, rather than just a single value.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8757 extends DLEP so a modem and router can exchange the minimum and maximum latency seen on a link. The range supplements the base protocol's single latency value.

questions: what is the dlep latency range extension
how does dlep report a latency range
what is dlep data item type 28
what units does the dlep latency range use
subtitle: A DLEP extension that reports the minimum and maximum latency on a link.

tldr.problem: The base DLEP latency item provides only one implementation-dependent latency value for a link.
tldr.mechanism: The Latency Range extension adds a data item with 64-bit maximum and minimum transmission delays, measured in microseconds.
tldr.outcome: DLEP peers can exchange a range of link latency alongside the existing latency item, following the same processing rules.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 8757's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC defines the DLEP Latency Range extension.

sections.title: Why Add a Latency Range
sections.content:
DLEP exchanges link-related control information between peers, which are a modem and a router. Its base specification includes one implementation-dependent latency value for a link.

This extension adds the ability to report the minimum and maximum latency that traffic can experience on that link. It does not change processing for the existing Latency Data Item.
sections.plainLanguage: The base protocol gives one latency value. This extension also reports the shortest and longest transmission delays seen on the link.

sections.title: The Latency Range Data Item
sections.content:
The data item has type 28 and length 16. It contains a 64-bit unsigned maximum-latency value followed by a 64-bit unsigned minimum-latency value.

Both values describe packet transmission delay over the link and are measured in microseconds. The data item must appear in the Session Initialization Response with default values for the session and may appear in other messages where the base latency item is allowed.
sections.plainLanguage: The data item carries two numbers in microseconds: the longest and shortest link delay. It is included during session initialization and can also accompany other permitted latency updates.

sections.title: Enabling the Extension
sections.content:
The use of the Latency Range extension should be configurable. An implementation indicates that it will use the extension by including extension type value 4 in the Extensions Supported Data Item.

The RFC says that this extension does not affect processing associated with the base Latency Data Item.
sections.plainLanguage: DLEP peers indicate support for the extension through the existing supported-extensions data item. The base latency value continues to be handled as before.
